proof.command: go build -o $TMPDIR/tester/smoke/dispatch-head5 ./cmd/dispatch; bash $TMPDIR/tester/smoke/owed-reply.sh <binary> <label> (creates a project, an issue and a comment mentioning session s1, marks the comment's index owed with `update comment_block_state set owed_at = now()`, fills in the session the listener would have claimed, then POSTs /api/v1/comments/{id}/reply naming block b2 as that session); and go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run 'TestACommentDeliveryReplyNamesABlockOfAnOwedComment|TestAMessageDeliveryReplyNamesABlockOfAnOwedMessage' -count=1

tenXCollapse.statement: At 10x BOTH builds collapse, so the transaction-id hold is the only 10x figure that separates them. Of 7,165 events offered in the window base committed 252 and head 254, that is 3.5 percent each, with 6,990 and 6,993 transport errors (client timeouts) and zero non-2xx on either side. No write latency is reported at 10x at all: the harness's per-kind write_ms is 0.0 for every kind on both builds, because almost no write was both answered and joined to a commit row in time. The live frame from the write's response is 0.0 for the same reason.
tenXCollapse.whatNotToRead: Dispatch RSS max at 10x reads 2,047.1 MiB at head against 1,973.1 at base, 3.8 percent. That is not a comparison: both builds are in collapse and the figure is taken over what survived two saturated runs. At 1x, which does not saturate, head's RSS is the lower of the two (3,382.9 against 3,405.8 MiB) and its write latency is better on both kinds. 10x offers ten times what this 2-CPU stack can serve; the hold is sampled from pg_stat_activity rather than bound by the offered rate, which is why it still separates the builds there.

unproven.evidence: Carried from round 3, where I measured it over five runs per build (head 674.1 ms against before-591 208.3 ms at p99, while head beat before-591 at p50 on that metric and at both percentiles measured from the event's creation). This round measured 1x and 10x against main, as the architect's brief named, so it adds no new reading. unproven.claim: A clean merge of main into this branch is not a safe merge, and nothing in CI enforces that.
unproven.evidence: The implementer records fifteen tests red at this round's first merge head that go build and go vet both passed, in three classes: a queued write a later read of the same transaction depended on, an artifacts row a read needed that the branch only queues, and a fixture holding a row where the branch now holds an owner lock. I verified the fixed state, not the discipline: whoever merges main into this branch again must run the api, docs, refs and pmdoc suites at the merge head, and no check makes them. It is a property of this branch's size against this repository's merge rate rather than a defect of the change.
